class.name: FauxStructuralFixture
class.brief_description: Test/sample bridge that builds committed synthetic structural fixtures and presents them to a [FauxBuildView].

description.para: [b]Fixture/sample infrastructure, not a production world-loading API.[/b] GDScript cannot carry a native [code]StructuralWorld[/code], so this class owns the one legitimate synthetic producer path: committed core fixture → core structural derivation → [code]StructuralWorld[/code] → [method present] hands it to the view's C++ production seam. [FauxBuildView] itself never constructs a world; this class never renders one.

[method present] accepts a committed fixture name only. Real-content (GRP/MAP) loading is out of scope for this harness. The [code]expected_*[/code] accessors expose the retained world's packed vertices/indices — derived independently of the view — as the expected side of consumer-boundary tests.
Names of the committed synthetic fixtures this harness can build.
Builds the named committed fixture, derives its structural world through the core, and presents it to [param view]. Returns [code]false[/code] and sets the last error on failure.

Serializes the named committed fixture through the core canonical MAP writer into [param directory] and returns the normalized VFS name of the written file (e.g. [code]SQUARE_ROOM.MAP[/code]); empty String with the last error set on failure. Test infrastructure: the production source route re-loads exactly these bytes through a directory mount.

Packs committed fixtures into a synthetic GRP archive in [param directory] using the approved M4 canonical builder, and returns the path written; empty String with the last error set on failure. Each entry is a Dictionary of [code]fixture[/code] (committed fixture name), [code]name[/code] (VFS entry name) and optional [code]corrupt[/code] (damages the serialized MAP payload while leaving the archive well-formed). Test infrastructure: it exists so the production [code]present_grp[/code] success path runs in CI on original synthetic content. Archive entry names are arbitrary VFS keys — no route behaviour is keyed off them.

Writes ORIGINAL synthetic assets — TILES000.ART, PALETTE.DAT and LOOKUP.DAT — into [param directory], so the textured production route can be driven end to end by committed content. The two tiles deliberately differ in dimensions, so a tile-size dependency in the UV authority is exercised rather than assumed away. Test infrastructure only.

Runs the core chain (mount, parse, derive, load assets, atlas, prepare) and retains the result, so the boundary test can compare what the [code]ArrayMesh[/code] holds against what core actually prepared. This is the EXPECTED side of the textured gate: it deliberately does not touch a view, so the view cannot satisfy the test with UVs of its own.
The prepared world's vertices in canonical prepared order, from the last [method prepare_from_dir].

The prepared world's UVs, one per vertex, in the same order as [method prepared_vertices]. Tile-local: 1.0 is one whole tile repeat, and values outside [code][0,1][/code] are normal and mean the tile tiles.
Human-readable description of the most recent failure, empty after a successful [method present].
Number of surfaces of [param kind] (core SurfaceKind order, Floor=0 .. PortalLower=4) in the retained world.
Vertices of all [param kind] surfaces in canonical order, packed independently of the view — the expected side of a consumer-boundary test.
Triangle indices of all [param kind] surfaces with accumulated vertex offsets, packed independently of the view.
Number of deferral notes carried by the retained world.
Number of nonfatal structural diagnostics (e.g. zero-area surfaces) in the retained world.
